userStories.title: Read-side tools never search .git or hang on special files
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Fix L14's grep half and L37a by excluding .git from fallback searches and refusing special-file reads without blocking.

**Motivation** — It searches `.git/`; the review's agent repro returned a token-bearing remote URL from `.git/config`.

**Approach** — `buildGrepArgv(binary, pattern, path, patternType?)` — Target: the `"grep"` branch returns `["grep", "-r", "-n", "--exclude-dir=.git", modeFlag, "--", pattern, target]`; the `"rg"` branch is unchanged.

`readPrefix(path: string, maxBytes: number): Promise<string>` — Target: same signature; opens with `constants.O_RDONLY | (constants.O_NONBLOCK ?? 0)` from `node:fs`, checks the opened handle's `stat().isFile()`, and when false closes the handle and throws `NaxError` code `READ_NOT_REGULAR_FILE`, message `"<path>" is not a regular file`, context `{ stage: "read", path }`. A regular file reads as today. nax-agent ships Node-compatible source, so this stays on `node:fs/promises`.

Failure handling: `readPrefix` on a FIFO, socket, directory or device rejects `READ_NOT_REGULAR_FILE` without blocking; `Read` returns `isError: true` with that message (its existing catch). Read `resolveWithin` and `getAgentRuntime().globSync` for context only; do not change them.

**Scope** — In: grep fallback argv and readPrefix, including real tool-level regression cases. Out: US-002 redaction/storage changes and US-008 chat-mention special-file handling. US-001 only: review L37b (`ScratchpadList` checks a glob hit against the repo root instead of the scratchpad) is dropped by evidence: both runtimes' `globSync` never return a symlink for a `**/*` pattern (Bun scans with `onlyFiles` and `followSymlinks: false`; `node-glob.ts` keeps a symlink only for a literal pattern), so no symlinked entry reaches the check. US-001 only: Bash writes to `.claude/settings.local.json` outside the OS sandbox (review L14's second half): the sandboxed path is already denied by `policy-builder.ts:212`. US-001 only: `readPrefix` on Windows: `O_NONBLOCK` is absent there and treated as `0`; FIFO behaviour on Windows is not tested. US-001 only: `readFileSlice` (`tools/read-file.ts:70`, behind `ScratchpadRead`) has the same open-without-type-check shape, but it only reads inside the agent's own scratchpad, so a FIFO there is one the agent made itself.

**Interface** — `buildGrepArgv(binary, pattern, path, patternType?)`; `readPrefix(path: string, maxBytes: number): Promise<string>`.

Testing: add cases to `packages/nax-agent/test/unit/tools/grep.test.ts` and `packages/nax-agent/test/unit/tools/buffering-ceilings.test.ts`, preserving existing assertions. Show a new fail-first case against old code; AC3, AC7 and AC9 are already-green regression guards.

[unit] buildGrepArgv("grep", "fo+|bar", undefined, "regex") returns an argv in which "--exclude-dir=.git" appears at an index lower than the index of "--".
[unit] buildGrepArgv("rg", "needle", undefined, "literal") returns an argv that omits "--exclude-dir=.git".

[unit] With _grepDeps.which returning null for "rg" (the grep fallback), grepTool.run with pattern "secret-marker-123" and no path, in a temp git repo whose .git/config and src/a.txt both hold "secret-marker-123", returns content with a row for src/a.txt and no row whose path includes the segment .git/.

[unit] readPrefix on a named pipe (FIFO) with no writer rejects within 2 seconds with a NaxError whose code is "READ_NOT_REGULAR_FILE" and whose message names the pipe's path; the test skips when the mkfifo utility is unavailable.
[unit] readPrefix on a directory rejects with a NaxError whose code is "READ_NOT_REGULAR_FILE".
[unit] readPrefix(path, 100) on a regular 500-byte file returns its first 101 bytes as UTF-8.

When readPrefix is given a FIFO, socket, directory or device, it rejects without blocking with READ_NOT_REGULAR_FILE rather than attempting to read its contents.

routing.reasoning: Small tool/helper changes, but preventing disclosure of credential-bearing git configuration is security-sensitive; FIFO rejection also needs real nonblocking filesystem tests.

userStories.title: Mask retained vendor secrets and write owner-only session files
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Fix L21 and L37c with the three specified secret patterns and 0600 session-content writes.

**Motivation** — `SECRET_VALUE_PATTERNS` (`packages/nax-agent/src/internal/redact.ts:43-122`) has no GitLab (`glpat-`), Google (`AIza`) or Stripe live (`sk_live_`, `rk_live_`) pattern; all pass `redactSecrets` unmasked.

**Approach** — `SECRET_VALUE_PATTERNS` — Target: three more entries after `aws`: `{ kind: "gitlab", re: /glpat-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}/g }`, `{ kind: "google", re: /AIza[0-9A-Za-z_-]{35}/g }`, `{ kind: "stripe", re: /\b[sr]k_live_[0-9A-Za-z]{16,}/g }`.

session file writers — Target: `writeTranscriptDoc`, `publishImageOnce` (through `_transcriptImagesDeps.writeFileAtomic`) and `archiveTranscript` pass `{ mode: 0o600 }` to `writeFileAtomic`; `writeMeta` passes `{ mode: 0o600 }` to `writeFile`. Directory modes are unchanged.

**Scope** — In: central redactor patterns and transcript/image/archive/metadata writer options, plus focused mode and redaction regression cases. Out: US-001 tool search/read behavior and US-005 orchestrator session reopen behavior. US-002 only: existing transcript, image, archive and session metadata files already on disk keep their mode until next written; directory modes are unchanged. US-002 only: Stripe test keys (`sk_test_`, `rk_test_`) and vendor key formats beyond `glpat-`, `AIza`, `sk_live_` and `rk_live_` are not added to the redactor.

**Interface** — Existing interfaces are read, not changed: `redactSecrets<T>(input: T): T`; `saveTranscript(dir, sessionName, messages, identity?)`, `transcriptPath(dir, sessionName)`, `transcriptImagesPath(path)`, `archiveTranscript(...)`, `createSessionStorage(deps).writeMeta(meta)`; `writeFileAtomic(path, content, { mode? })`.

Testing: create `packages/nax-agent/test/unit/native/transcript-store-modes.test.ts` for transcript, image and archive modes; append metadata coverage to `packages/nax-agent/test/unit/session-store/storage-hardening.test.ts` and redaction cases to the existing redaction suite. Assert real permission bits, including replacing an existing 0644 transcript. No existing assertion changes are needed. AC6 is an already-green guard; demonstrate at least one new failure on old code.

userStories.title: Preserve pi-stream usage after unparseable tool arguments
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Fix L28 by draining a malformed-tool stream to its terminal usage before emitting one bad-request error.

**Motivation** — In `createPiProtocol` (`packages/nax-ai/src/protocols/pi-client.ts:349-368`) a `toolcall_end` whose arguments fail to parse yields a `bad-request` error and returns before the terminal event's usage, so the hop's tokens are lost.

**Approach** — `createPiProtocol(...).stream`, `toolcall_end` case — Target: when `parseToolArgs` throws, remember the `bad-request` error (same message and cause as today) instead of yielding it and enter a draining state. While draining, every event other than `done` and `error` is ignored. On `done`: yield `{ type: "usage", usage: toTokenUsage(event.message.usage) }`, then the remembered error, then return (no `done`). On upstream `error`: as today, yield the upstream usage when `totalTokens(usage) > 0`, then run the existing abort check (an aborted request signal still throws its abort), then yield the remembered error instead of the upstream one, then return. If the upstream iterator ends while draining, yield the remembered error after the loop. If the upstream iterator throws while draining, the existing catch rethrows an abort as today; otherwise it yields the remembered error instead of the classified throw. A stream never yields more than one `error` event. The drain is bounded by the request's own timeout and abort signal, as the rest of the stream already is.

**Scope** — In: pi protocol's parse-failure stream state and scripted event regression cases. Out: US-002 credential redaction and storage, US-005 ACP session/turn budgets, and consumer-level cost or retry changes.

**Interface** — `createPiProtocol(...).stream`; existing `toTokenUsage`, `totalTokens` are read, not changed. Error message remains `Tool "read" returned unparseable arguments.` for tool read.

Testing: create `packages/nax-ai/test/protocols/pi-client-tool-args.test.ts` — the US-003 cases; `pi-client.test.ts` is already 984 lines. Copy its `drain`, `message`, `fakePi`, `BASE` and `MODEL` helpers. Do not modify the existing unparseable-arguments assertion: its first text delta and final bad-request remain valid. AC2, AC3, AC5, AC6 and AC8 are already-green guards; AC1/AC4/AC7 provide fail-first behavior. Scripted events prove mapping, not actual provider behavior.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] A pi stream of text_delta, toolcall_delta with delta '{"path"', toolcall_end, then done whose message usage reports 100 input and 20 output tokens yields a usage event with inputTokens: 100 and outputTokens: 20, and its final event is an error with kind: "bad-request" that comes after that usage event.
[unit] The stream in AC1 yields no tool-call event and no done event.
[unit] A pi stream of toolcall_delta with delta '{"path"', toolcall_end, a second text_delta, then done yields no text-delta event for the second delta.

[unit] A pi stream of toolcall_delta with delta '{"path"', toolcall_end, then an upstream error event whose usage reports 50 input tokens yields a usage event with inputTokens: 50, then exactly one error event, with kind: "bad-request" and the message Tool "read" returned unparseable arguments.

[unit] A pi stream of toolcall_delta with delta '{"path"' and toolcall_end, after which the upstream iterator ends with no done or error event, yields as its final event an error with kind: "bad-request" and yields no usage event.
[unit] A pi stream whose tool arguments parse yields the tool-call event, then usage, then done.
[unit] A pi stream of toolcall_delta with delta '{"path"', toolcall_end, then an upstream error event, read with a request signal that is already aborted, rejects with the signal's abort reason.

[unit] A pi stream of toolcall_delta with delta '{"path"' and toolcall_end, after which the upstream iterator throws a non-abort Error("socket reset"), yields exactly one error event, with kind: "bad-request".

routing.reasoning: One existing protocol generator gains a remembered-error drain state with fully specified terminal branches; scripted PiDeps fixtures support focused fail-first tests without a new abstraction or integration.

suggestedCriteria: When the upstream iterator throws while draining and the request signal is aborted, consuming createPiProtocol(...).stream rejects with that abort rather than emitting a bad-request error.

userStories.title: Release crashed-run locks and preserve tracked .env worktree files
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Fix L1 and L2 by releasing owned locks on fatal teardown and retaining checked-out .env files in new worktrees.

**Motivation** — A holder with the same PID counts as alive, so a restart that reuses the PID (a container's PID 1) is refused.

**Approach** — `CrashRecoveryContext` / `SignalHandlerContext` — Target: new optional field `releaseLocks?: () => Promise<void>`. Each of the three fatal handlers (signal, uncaught exception, unhandled rejection) awaits `ctx.releaseLocks?.()` after `clearHiddenNaxIndexFlags(ctx)` and before `cancelDeadline()` and `_crashSignalsDeps.exit(...)`, so the teardown deadline still bounds it; a rejection is caught and logged at warn, and the exit code is unchanged.

`setupRun` (`execution/lifecycle/run-setup.ts`) — Target: passes `releaseLocks: async () => { await releaseRunLocks?.(); }` to `installCrashHandlers`, a forwarder over a local `releaseRunLocks` that stays `undefined` until BOTH the checkout lock and the feature lock are acquired, and is then set to release the feature lock (`releaseFeatureLock({ outputDir: runtime.outputDir, feature, runId })`) and then `releaseLock(workdir)`. The same pattern as the existing `sealApprovals` forwarder. `run-setup.ts` is 582 lines against the 600-line limit; if the change would cross it, move the lock-acquisition block into a helper module.

`WorktreeManager.create(projectRoot, worktreeId)` — Target: when `<worktreePath>/.env` already exists (checked with `lstat`), skip the symlink and log at debug `".env is tracked; the worktree keeps the checked-out copy"`; otherwise symlink as today.

**Scope** — In: fatal context forwarding/consumption, lock ownership timing and worktree .env destination handling. Out: US-005 session reopen/turn-loop changes and US-006 workflow abort propagation. US-004 only: a run killed by `SIGKILL` or the OOM killer still leaves its locks; only the catchable fatal paths release them. US-004 only: a fatal signal that arrives after normal cleanup released the locks but before the crash handlers are removed may release again; `releaseFeatureLock` checks the runId and the checkout-lock unlink tolerates a missing file. Review L3 (feature-lock reclaim has no `.reclaim` mutex) is dropped by ruling: it needs three nax runs racing for one feature lock.

**Interface** — `releaseLocks?: () => Promise<void>` on both context interfaces; `setupRun`; `WorktreeManager.create(projectRoot, worktreeId)`. Read, do not change: `releaseLock(workdir)` (unconditional unlink) and `releaseFeatureLock({ outputDir, feature, runId })` (leaves a different runId's lock).

Testing: drive the installed signal/exception/rejection handlers, and create `packages/nax/test/unit/execution/lifecycle/run-setup-crash-locks.test.ts` by mirroring the approvals-seal capture-context pattern. Integration AC7-AC9 must call the setupRun-produced captured forwarder, including before either/both acquisitions succeed; AC10-AC12 use real temporary git worktrees. AC4, AC5, AC11 and AC12 already pass before the fix and remain guards. No existing assertion changes are needed.

[unit] The uncaught-exception handler installed by installSignalHandlers(ctx) calls ctx.releaseLocks exactly once, before _crashSignalsDeps.exit(1).
[unit] The unhandled-rejection handler installed by installSignalHandlers(ctx) calls ctx.releaseLocks exactly once, before _crashSignalsDeps.exit(1).
[unit] When ctx.releaseLocks rejects, the SIGTERM handler still calls _crashSignalsDeps.exit(143).
[unit] With no ctx.releaseLocks, the SIGTERM handler calls _crashSignalsDeps.exit(143).
[unit] The SIGTERM handler calls ctx.releaseLocks after ctx.statusWriter has recorded the crashed status.

[integration] setupRun in a temp workdir with real checkout and feature locks, where _runSetupDeps.installCrashHandlers is stubbed to capture its context and the run setup completes, then calling the captured releaseLocks() removes nax.lock from the workdir, and a following acquireFeatureLock for the same feature with a different runId returns acquired: true.

[integration] setupRun where _runSetupDeps.acquireFeatureLock returns { acquired: false, holder } (setup throws), then a nax.lock written by another holder, then calling the captured releaseLocks(), leaves that nax.lock in place.

When ctx.releaseLocks rejects in a fatal handler, that handler logs the rejection at warn before exiting with its unchanged fatal exit code.

routing.reasoning: Cross-module fatal teardown and acquisition-timed ownership forwarding require integration checks for destructive lock release, plus independent worktree behavior.

userStories.title: Close aborted sessions on reopen and stop interactions at the turn cap
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Fix L4 and L5 by closing cancelled live handles before reopening and never asking for another prompt after the last allowed turn.

**Motivation** — A `keepOpen` turn aborted mid-flight leaves the descriptor `FAILED` (`:598-602`) with the adapter session still open, so the old agent process runs until the end-of-run sweep.

**Approach** — `SessionManager.openSessionImpl` — Target: when a live handle exists and its name is in `_cancelledSessions` (the turn was aborted), the reopen closes it with `this.closeSession(liveHandle, true)` instead of only dropping it. A terminal descriptor that was not cancelled keeps today's drop (its adapter session is already closed). `session/manager.ts` is grandfathered at 650 lines and may not grow: fold the condition into the existing `close-then-reopen` branch.

`runLoop` — Target: after `state.output = outcome.output`, `if (used(state) >= loop.max) break;` before `nextPrompt`, so no human question or context-tool request is issued after the last allowed turn.

**Scope** — In: SessionManager cancelled-handle cleanup and ACP turn-loop interaction timing. Out: US-002 session file permissions, US-003 pi stream draining, US-004 run-lock fatal cleanup and US-006 workflow-level abort adjudication. Do not redesign endpoint identity or normal terminal-descriptor reuse policy. Review L37d (session-lock same-PID takeover and the ACP registry `session/load` race) is dropped by ruling: it needs a reused PID or two concurrent loads of one session.

**Interface** — `SessionManager.openSessionImpl`; `runLoop`; existing callers `SessionManager.openSession(name, opts)`, `sendPrompt`, `closeSession(handle, true)` and `runTurnLoop(session, prompt, opts)` retain their signatures.

Testing: use existing session manager/endpoint fixtures and `packages/nax/test/unit/agents/acp/turn-loop.test.ts` helpers `scriptedOpened`, `replyTurn` and `answering`. Check adapter close-before-open call order, cancelled-marker reset, close failure tolerance and question/context-tool exhaustion. Preserve existing assertions; AC2, AC3 and AC4 are already-green guards and a new case must fail against old code.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] SessionManager.openSession(name, opts), then sendPrompt whose adapter sendTurn rejects with an AbortError while the signal is aborted, then openSession(name, opts) again, calls the adapter's closeSession exactly once with the first handle, before the adapter's second openSession call.
[unit] SessionManager.openSession(name, opts), a successful sendPrompt, closeSession(handle, true), then openSession(name, opts) again calls the adapter's closeSession exactly once in total.
[unit] After the abort-then-reopen sequence of AC1, sendPrompt on the new handle resolves with the adapter's turn result instead of throwing SESSION_CANCELLED.
[unit] After the abort-then-reopen sequence of AC1 with an adapter whose closeSession rejects, the second openSession still resolves to a new handle.

[unit] runTurnLoop with maxInteractions: 2, a handler answering "a" and "b", and an agent whose every reply is a question calls onInteraction exactly once and sends exactly two prompts.
[unit] runTurnLoop with maxInteractions: 3, a handler answering "a", "b" and "c", and an agent whose every reply is a question calls onInteraction exactly twice.
[unit] runTurnLoop with maxInteractions: 1 where the agent's reply is a context-tool call calls onInteraction zero times.

routing.reasoning: Two localized lifecycle fixes use existing abstractions, but cancelled-session ownership and reopening trigger the mandatory sessions security override.

userStories.title: Honor workflow abort during CI waits and residual adjudication
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Fix L6 and L10 by waking CI waits promptly on abort and propagating aborted advisor failures without default-hold ledger writes.

**Motivation** — `adjudicateResidual` (`workflow/adjudicate.ts:8-36`) catches every advisor error, including an abort, writes default-hold rulings to the ledger and returns, so an aborted story is closed as if adjudicated.

**Approach** — `_ciWaitDeps.sleep` — Baseline: `(ms: number) => Promise<void>` over `Bun.sleep`. Target: `(ms: number, signal?: AbortSignal) => Promise<void>` that resolves when `ms` elapses or as soon as `signal` aborts (built on `cancellableDelay`, with the abort rejection turned into a resolve). `waitWithHeartbeat` takes `opts.signal`, passes it to every `_ciWaitDeps.sleep` call and stops slicing once it is aborted; the loop's existing top-of-loop check then returns `end("pending", "aborted")`.

`adjudicateResidual(advisor, req, ledger, aborted?: () => boolean)` — Target: in the catch, when `aborted?.()` is true, rethrow the advisor's error before any default hold or ledger write. `StoryLoopEnv` gains `readonly aborted?: () => boolean`; `buildStoryEnv` (`workflow/stage-env.ts:49`) sets it to `() => ctx.abortSignal?.aborted === true`; `residualStep` passes `env.aborted`; `buildFeatureEnv`'s `adjudicate` passes `() => fc.runSignal?.aborted === true`.

**Scope** — In: CI sleep/heartbeat signal propagation and residual-adjudication abort predicate across story/feature environments. Out: US-004 fatal teardown and lock cleanup and US-005 adapter session cleanup. Review L7 (`workflow promote` binds the CI wait to local HEAD) is dropped by ruling: it fails closed as `unavailable`. Review L13 (a failed CI poll from an older head SHA is terminal) is dropped by ruling: a GitLab timing edge, rated plausible.

**Interface** — `(ms: number, signal?: AbortSignal) => Promise<void>`; `adjudicateResidual(advisor, req, ledger, aborted?: () => boolean)`; `StoryLoopEnv` gains `readonly aborted?: () => boolean`. Existing `cancellableDelay(ms, signal?)` is read, not changed, and rejects on abort. Optional additions preserve existing builders and one-argument sleep stubs.

Testing: add behavior cases to existing workflow suites, proving both producers and consumers: default sleep, waitForChecks, direct adjudication, residualStep, runStoryLoop, buildStoryEnv and buildFeatureEnv. The runStoryLoop case must reach residual adjudication after maxFixRounds and assert no closed update, not only a helper rejection. Preserve existing assertions; AC2, AC4, AC7 and AC8 are already-green guards, and at least one new AC must fail against old code.

userStories.title: Create new PRs for closed branches and fail deferred review on diff errors
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Fix L12 and L29 so closed/merged PRs are not reused and failed git diffs cannot masquerade as no changes.

**Motivation** — `gh pr view <branch>` also returns a CLOSED or MERGED PR, which is then reported `already-ready` with a dead URL; the function's own doc says a closed PR should lead to a new one.

**Approach** — `parseView(stdout, forge)` — Baseline: returns `{ isDraft: boolean; url?: string }`. Target: returns `{ isDraft: boolean; url?: string; closed: boolean }`, `closed` true when GitHub's `state` is `"CLOSED"` or `"MERGED"`, or GitLab's `state` is `"closed"` or `"merged"`; false when `state` is absent or anything else. `openOrPromotePr` (both view calls) requests GitHub fields `"isDraft,url,state"`. A view that succeeds with `closed: true` is handled exactly like a failed view: the non-`keepDraft` path creates the PR (`opened`), the `keepDraft` path creates a draft (`draft`).

`spawnGitWithDeadline` — Target: returns `{ stdout: string; exitCode: number; timedOut: boolean }`. `captureRunStartRef` returns `""` unless `exitCode === 0` and not timed out. `getChangedFilesForDeferred` returns `{ ok: true; files: string[] } | { ok: false; error: string }`, the error naming `git diff` and the exit code (or `timed out`). On `ok: false`, `runDeferredReview` calls no reviewer and returns `changedFiles: []`, `anyFailed: true` and one `reviewerResults` entry per reviewer with `passed: false`, `output: ""` and `error` set to that message.

**Scope** — In: forge-state parsing/creation and deferred-review git failure results. Out: US-004 worktree creation, US-006 abort-aware workflow waits and US-009 quality-command drains. userStories.description:
**Goal** — Fix L17 and L18 by avoiding special-file content reads and reading only a bounded background-log tail.

**Motivation** — `BackgroundTaskRegistry.output` (`chat/background/task-registry.ts:254-267`) reads the whole log (up to `TASK_LOG_MAX_BYTES`, 50 MiB) through `_backgroundTaskDeps.readLog` to return at most 500 lines.

**Approach** — `_mentionExpandDeps.stat` — Baseline: returns `{ isDirectory: boolean; size: number }`. Target: returns `{ isDirectory: boolean; size: number; special?: true }`; the default sets `special: true` only when the path is neither a regular file nor a directory (FIFO, socket, device) and omits the key otherwise, so existing test stubs that return `{ isDirectory, size }` keep modelling regular files. `contentRecord` returns `pathOnly(located.path, "path only: not a regular file")` for a special path, before any read.

`_backgroundTaskDeps.readLog` — Target: same signature `(path: string) => Promise<string>`; the default reads at most the last `TASK_LOG_TAIL_BYTES` (new exported constant, 2 MiB) through `Bun.file(path).slice(start)`, and when it started mid-file and the byte before the slice is not a newline, drops everything up to and including the first newline of the slice, so the result starts on a line boundary; a slice with no newline is returned as is. A file at or under the cap is read whole. `output()` is unchanged.

**Scope** — In: mention stat classification/content refusal and the default background-log reader. Out: US-001 agent Read/grep changes, US-002 redaction/storage permissions and US-009 subprocess drains. Preserve mention path-security/ignore policy, TASK_LOG_MAX_BYTES write ceiling and output() line selection/notice behavior.

**Interface** — `_mentionExpandDeps.stat` returns `{ isDirectory: boolean; size: number; special?: true }`; `_backgroundTaskDeps.readLog`: `(path: string) => Promise<string>`; exported `TASK_LOG_TAIL_BYTES` equals `2 * 1024 * 1024`. userStories.title: Bound post-exit quality drains and keep rectifier output tails
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Fix L16 and L34 by separating leader exit from bounded pipe draining and retaining failure summaries in rectifier prompts.

**Motivation** — A background child that keeps the pipe open (`sleep 20 & echo lint-clean`) holds the drain until the kill timer fires, turning a passing command into `timedOut: true`.

**Approach** — `runSingleCommand` stream collection — Target: `STREAM_DRAIN_TIMEOUT_MS` (2 000) is exported, and the drain deadlines are armed and cleared through `_qualityRunnerDeps.setTimeout` / `_qualityRunnerDeps.clearTimeout` so tests can fire them. On the non-timeout path the kill timer is cleared as soon as the leader exits, before the drain, so it cannot fire during the drain window. stdout and stderr are collected chunk by chunk, so the text read so far is available at any moment. After the leader exits, on both the timeout and the non-timeout path, each stream gets `STREAM_DRAIN_TIMEOUT_MS` to finish; at the deadline the text read so far is used. On the non-timeout path, when a stream missed the deadline, the process group is sent `SIGTERM` through `_qualityRunnerDeps.killProcessGroup(proc.pid, "SIGTERM", { singleProcessFallback: false })` so the pipe-holding child does not outlive the call. `success`, `exitCode` and `timedOut: false` come from the leader's exit as today.

`capText` — Target: replaced by exported `capTail(value: string, maxChars: number): string` in `rectifier-builder-helpers.ts`. At or under `maxChars` it returns `value`. Over it, it keeps the last `maxChars` characters, drops a leading partial line when the kept text has a newline before its last character, and prefixes `... (truncated — ${value.length} chars total; showing the last ${kept.length})\n`. `formatCheckError`, `renderCheckBlock` and the `noOpReprompt` loop use `capTail` with their existing limits (1 000 / 4 000). `rectifier-builder.ts` is grandfathered at 751 lines and may not grow; the two inline cuts collapse to calls.

**Scope** — In: quality command stream lifecycle/timers and shared rectifier tail formatting. Out: US-003 pi usage draining, US-007 deferred-review git failures and US-008 background log-tail reading. Preserve existing real command timeout escalation, trust checking and leader-derived exit result.

**Interface** — Export `STREAM_DRAIN_TIMEOUT_MS` (2 000) from `quality/runner.ts`; export `capTail(value: string, maxChars: number): string` from `rectifier-builder-helpers.ts`. The latter's consumers are `RectifierPromptBuilder.firstAttemptDelta`, `noOpReprompt` and `reviewRectification`; AC10-AC12 exercise those connections.

Testing: create `packages/nax/test/unit/quality/runner-drain.test.ts` — the US-009 runner cases; `runner.test.ts` is 695 lines. Use injectable timers for immediate drain-deadline tests and real shell commands for the integration cases, retaining partial output and preventing orphaned pipe-holding children. Append builder cases to `packages/nax/test/unit/prompts/builders/rectifier-builder.test.ts` and helper cases to the existing helper suite without changing existing assertions. AC3, AC4, AC6 and AC8 are already-green guards; demonstrate at least one new fail-first AC.
